$comment: Single source of truth for the support matrix. Run `dotnet run --project build/Tools -- coverage` after editing; CI verifies README.md matches.

entries.name: UBL 2.1 — Invoice
entries.notes: Reading and writing the EN 16931 core, with everything else kept verbatim as extension data. Round-tripped against the 45 UBL invoices of the official XRechnung test suite without losing an element. Validation comes with the rule engine.

entries.name: UBL 2.1 — Credit Note
entries.notes: In UBL a credit note is not an invoice with a different code: it has its own root element and renames three things inside it. Read, written and round-tripped against the official EN 16931 credit note, and the type code (BT-3) decides which root a document built in code is written under.

entries.name: UN/CEFACT CII
entries.notes: Reading and writing the EN 16931 core, with everything else kept verbatim as extension data on the node that contained it. Round-tripped against the 41 CII invoices of the official XRechnung test suite without losing an element.

entries.name: UN/CEFACT CDAR
entries.notes: The generic message, which is what makes the fallback real: a national profiling this library does not know still parses, with its codes uninterpreted and the downgrade reported. Validation runs any Schematron rule set published for it, the French BR-FR-CDV included.

entries.name: EN 16931 (core invoice model)
entries.notes: The published Schematron artefacts are executed as data. Measured against the 23 official example documents and the 80 CIUS documents of the XRechnung test suite: all accepted.

entries.name: Factur-X / ZUGFeRD — MINIMUM → EXTENDED
entries.notes: All five profiles registered. MINIMUM and BASIC WL are read and reported as not being EN 16931 invoices (EIV4010) rather than silently accepted.

entries.name: Factur-X hybrid PDF
entries.notes: Embeds the CII payload into a PDF you already produce, and extracts it back, with the Factur-X XMP metadata. Rendering a PDF and converting one to PDF/A-3 are out of scope: those are properties of the document you start from.

entries.name: Peppol BIS Billing
entries.notes: The profiles for both syntaxes, the EN 16931 electronic address scheme list taken from the artefacts this library ships, and participant identifiers. The Peppol rules declare no licence and are therefore fetched, not packaged — one call loads all four once they are: AddPeppolRulesFrom(directory). The engine agrees with every case of Peppol's own unit corpus, 227 of 227 for UBL and 127 of 127 for CII.

entries.name: XRechnung (CIUS + Extension)
entries.notes: Profiles for both syntaxes and the published rule sets, embedded. Measured against all 86 documents of the official KoSIT test suite.

entries.name: France — invoicing (CIUS FR, Factur-X)
entries.notes: The conformant extension urn.cpro.gouv.fr:1p0:extended-ctc-fr, the invoicing case (BT-23) and the three mentions French law requires, with the SIREN of both parties checked before it is written. An invoice built with ForFrance() satisfies EN 16931, BR-FR-Flux2 and EXTENDED-CTC-FR in both syntaxes, measured on every build.

entries.name: France — lifecycle statuses (CDAR)
entries.notes: Every status, to a trading partner and to the public portal, measured on each build against the DGFiP's own BR-FR-CDV rules and their eleven sample messages. The artefacts are fetched, not shipped: run build/fetch-specs.sh france.

entries.name: France — legal identifiers (SIREN, SIRET, VAT)
entries.notes: SIREN, SIRET and VAT numbers with their check digits, including the La Poste establishments that satisfy a different rule from Luhn.

entries.name: France — e-reporting (flux 10)
entries.notes: The transactions and payments transmissions, built, written and read back. The DGFiP publishes no sample transmissions, so what is measured is that every document this library builds satisfies the published flux 10 rules.

entries.name: Germany — XRechnung, ZUGFeRD, Leitweg-ID
entries.notes: XRechnung profiles for both syntaxes, the Leitweg-ID with its check digit, and the published rule sets running against the official test suite.

entries.name: Belgium — Peppol BIS, KBO/BCE, structured communication
entries.notes: Built on International.EInvoicing.Peppol, which the 2026 mandate is: the KBO/BCE enterprise number with its modulo 97 check, the structured communication, and Peppol validation once the artefacts are fetched.

entries.name: Rest of the world
entries.notes: Some fifty countries, catalogued in the roadmap below by what each would cost to add: a rule set and an identifier for the Peppol ones, a reader and a writer for the national formats, a different document entirely for the clearance countries.

entries.name: Peppol AS4, French PA APIs, Chorus Pro, Mercurius
entries.notes: This library produces and reads documents. Sending them is your access point's job.

entries.name: PDF rendering and PDF/A conversion
entries.notes: A hybrid invoice starts from the PDF you produce for humans. Building that PDF, and making it PDF/A-conforming, belongs to your reporting or PDF library.
